rules.says: __PRESENT__ is selected without its twin __ABSENT__. The two cover one rule in different ways, so select both.
__PRESENT__ check the same commands from one shared table. Keep one, or a command is checked twice.
__PRESENT__ refuses every new dependency until __FILE__ exists (not found in the current directory). Create it first.
__PRESENT__ refuses every MCP server until __FILE__ exists (not found in the current directory). Create it first.
__PRESENT__ warns only, being measured (observe): nothing is refused.
__PRESENT__ is text only: nothing stops a violation (advisory).
__PRESENT__ is also in the chock plugin __PLUGIN__ (__PATH__), so both copies fire. Remove it from one of the two selections.
Codex skips a plugin's hooks until you review and trust them in /hooks, and asks again after a hook changes: until then every policy here is advisory.
Devin runs plugin hooks on a best-effort basis. A hook that errors or times out lets the action through.
This client names no file-write tool a hook can match. So a gate checks what a turn wrote only at turn end, and it does not stop the write when it happens.
In Copilot CLI, a gate checks the write before it lands (seen in a live run on 2026-10-11, CLI 1.0.94 on Windows). In VS Code agent mode that is unmeasured.
On Cursor Teams and Enterprise an admin setting (Allow Local Plugin Imports) can turn local plugins off, and an installed marketplace plugin of the same name takes precedence over this one.
goose denies a PreToolUse call when its hook fails, because every entry sets `on_failure: block`. Its Stop hooks keep the default, so if a gate fails at turn end, the turn still finishes.

If a Grok hook times out, crashes or returns malformed output, the action goes through. Only an explicit deny blocks, and an allowManagedHooksOnly policy skips plugin hooks. No gate runs here, because agentseam records neither a write-tool vocabulary nor a blocking Stop for grok.
Antigravity documents no fail mode for a hook and no plugin-root variable. The hooks name the plugin folder by absolute path, and a gate checks what a turn wrote only at turn end.

On Windows, goose runs every hook with `sh -c`, so Git for Windows' sh must be on PATH. Without it, every tool call is denied, even a harmless one, because the hook cannot start (`on_failure: block`).

OpenHands documents no plugin-root variable: the hooks name the plugin folder by absolute path, and its hook runner blocks only on exit code 2 or a deny, so any other hook failure lets the call through.
Evidence wanted: what you see OpenHands do with this plugin, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/181

Kimi Code lets a call through when a hook errors, times out or exits with any code other than 2. It cannot prompt, so an ask is not enforced there. It applies a plugin to every project you open. It installs from its TUI only and runs a copy, so reinstall after a rebuild.
On Windows, the shell Kimi Code runs hook commands with is unmeasured, and the hooks read ${KIMI_PLUGIN_ROOT}. This path is not tested there.

Factory Droid treats a hook exit other than 0 or 2 as a non-blocking error and lets the call through, ignores this plugin's hooks under an org's allowManagedHooksOnly, and (agentseam's vendor data) degrades an ask to a block.
Evidence wanted: what you see Kimi Code do with this plugin, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/135
Evidence wanted: what you see Factory Droid do with this plugin, at https://github.com/open-coder-ai/agentseam/issues/184
Untested: chock has not seen an install work in this client in a live run. Its steps, its hooks and the plugin version string (<bundle.version>+<digest12>) are unmeasured there.
